objections: It is not runbook compliance, it is an amendment made after seeing the result. Step 3's v12 bullet says 'A fail keeps both filters'. The proposed wet run carries neither filter: no "R0w" in exclude_rules and no exclude_released at all. Re-wording the fail branch to 'every wet run of an UNJUDGED plan' narrows a pre-committed consequence after the fact. It also breaks house precedent: 552 unit 1 left 17 judged-right withheld heads unshipped, and v9/v12 called release_withheld's judged rights an 'accepted cost'. The distinction that saves it is real but has to be argued and recorded. Those were HOLDS the rule makes. These are planned CHANGES that the filter only defers until they are judged.

In substance it is safer than a pass, but only for a fixed set of labels. The 79 are a strict subset of what a pass would have shipped (all 81, including up to 1 known wrong), and the filters stay on afterwards. But with both filters off, the single per-item label becomes the only safety layer, and this class's labels are demonstrably noisy. Plan 2543's re-judge (rejudge2543_result.json) read both of today's wrongs as not-wrong: 4040 'right', its own text noting the 'WIMED Sp. z o.o. (dawniej WIMED 4.0 …)' print, and 22678568 'neutral'. That is 0 of 2 agreement on the wrong boundary. With a judge miss rate m, the residual wrongs among the shipped rights are about 2m/(1-m). This matches the pass's tolerance only if m is about 1/3 or less, and nothing yet measures m.

The 16-item blind second reading is too small and gates nothing. At this class's ~3-4% wrong rate, 16 items are expected to hold about 0.5 wrongs. Zero findings bounds the miss rate only at about 17% (95%). The proposal also does not say what result prunes or stops the run. The skeptic-on-every-wrong protocol is one-sided: it can only turn wrongs into rights, so every 'right' got exactly one reading.
Shipping the 1 released neutral has no upside by definition. Neutral is also the boundary class where readings flip (22678568 went neutral -> wrong).

One job is one undo unit. revert-org-name-refresh refuses org_ids, so there is no per-org or per-class revert. A single wrong found after the apply forces reverting all 79 or keeping it. Putting R0w (4 items, the head's own words, near zero risk), the 52 control-only releases and the 23 other unfit releases in one job ties their undo together.

Plan identity is not checked. The wet run reads latest_report("org-name-refresh-plan") and checks only epoch, rev, as_of, undated, stopped, truncated and scope (supervisor.rs org_name_refresh_targets). Any dry plan enqueued in between silently replaces 2569, and a SCOPED one is accepted by a scoped (org_ids) wet run. A deploy changes the rev and is refused, and 551 unit 3 is mid-flight toward a deploy. After an abort and re-plan, the same id list would apply the NEW plan's new_name, which may differ from the judged spelling.

Drift is safe by construction, so this is a timing point, not a safety one. read_readiness marks a target Ready only on the same rule label and a byte-identical new_name, and the window's compare-and-set keys on the pre-image, so drift never ships an unjudged spelling. The drift limit is max(79/50, 5) = 5: 6 or more drifted or gone aborts with nothing written. The ~07:00 UTC ingest adds the mentions that move elections. It is now ~00:00 UTC, so there are about 6 h of margin.

'The 2 wrongs simply stay held' is only true for a while. exclude_released matches the entry's recent_released, so it holds them only while they remain junk releases. 22678568's head was printed only on 2024-07-10, so its head_current hold lapses around 2027-07-10. 'MZP-Ingenieure' then becomes a plain R1 change that no v12 filter drops. 4040 lapses around 2029-07. Canary readings compare verdict:reason only (change:R1 either way), so a canary cannot flag this. R0w heads lapse the same way (552 unit 2 point 6: 22661109 around 2027-08). That is neutral against not shipping them, because the raw head's hold lapses identically.

Unit 2c (the weekly auto-run) is not built: there is no scheduler code for a wet refresh. The runbook text it would inherit says it carries only exclude_rules R2. Built from that text, it would ship the 2 wrongs and every new unjudged unfit release and R0w.

The next plan will read as a 'port bug'. Step 2's v12 GO bullet expects about 4 R0w (22289866, 22661109, 22981989, 23474998 among them), recent_released.unfit about 77 and by_rule.R1 about 77. After this run the next plan reads about 0 R0w, about 2 unfit releases plus new ones, and about 4 more holds (the collapsed R0w heads, now fit, held by recent/residue/head_current per the durability test). Unless the bullet is re-based, the next operator stops on a false alarm, or worse, talks themselves past a real one.

The post-apply dated check of 30 applied_samples is not independent. The samples are drawn from the same 79 census-judged items, so it is a partial third reading. The proposal states no bar for it. No canary or test conflicts: none of the 81 ids is among the 60 ORG_NAME_REFRESH_CANARIES, and the R0w pins in supervisor.rs and head_election.rs are fixture strings, unaffected by prod renames.

decision.why:
In substance this is not a loophole. The 79 ids are a strict subset of what a pass would have shipped (all 81 R0w and unfit changes, including up to 1 known wrong). The filters also stay on every later rule-driven run, which a pass would have lifted. So on a fixed set of labels it is safer on both counts.

Procedurally, though, it rewrites a pre-committed fail branch after seeing the result. The proposed run omits both filters that 'a fail keeps both filters' names, and the house has so far treated forgone judged-right fixes as accepted cost. It is defensible because these are planned changes the filter only defers until judged, not holds. But it has to be recorded as a decision, with its acceptance rule fixed before more evidence comes in.

The real risk moves from the rule to the judge. With the filters off, a single reading per item is the only safety layer, and on the wrong boundary the plan-2543 reading agreed with today's on 0 of the 2 wrongs. A 16-item blind reading with no gate cannot bound that. A blind re-read of all 79, with agreement required, can.

The mechanics checked out in code (supervisor.rs org_name_refresh_targets, head_election.rs read_readiness and org_name_refresh_drift_limit):
- org_ids with exclude_rules [R2] and no exclude_released puts the listed unfit releases and R0w in scope.
- Drift can only skip a target, never ship an unjudged spelling: the pre-pass needs the same rule and a byte-identical new_name, and the write compares and sets on the pre-image.
- 79 ids abort at 6 or more drifted or gone, with nothing written.
- No canary or test expects these ids held.

The gaps that remain:
- The wet run never checks which stored plan it is applying (only epoch and rev).
- Undo is whole-job only, hence the split into class jobs.
- The 2 wrongs and the R0w heads stay protected only until their head_current holds lapse (from about 2027-07). After that no filter catches them.
- Unit 2c, the weekly run, is not built yet, and the runbook text it would inherit carries only exclude_rules R2.
- The runbook's step-2 v12 expectations will misfire on the next plan unless they are re-based.
